question: Does the Silago coastal fishery profile provide a taxonomically usable species inventory for Southern Leyte?

sourceReviewed.citation: Amor, M. F. N. E., & Pesquera, N. M. (2014). Fish Profile of Barangays Tubaon, District II, Mercedes and Balagawanin Silago, Southern Leyte. Journal of Science, Engineering and Technology, 2(1), 135-145. https://doi.org/10.61569/h5sg5910
sourceReviewed.access: Reviewed the official Southern Leyte State University journal record and the full 11-page article PDF mirrored by Semantic Scholar. The PDF mirror was used only to inspect the article; no copy was added to the repository.

reportedScope.localities: Four selected coastal barangays in Silago, Southern Leyte: Tubaon/Tuba-on, District II, Mercedes, and Balagawan (the title uses ‘Balagawanin’). The study describes Silago Sea fishing grounds but provides no point-level fishing coordinates.
reportedScope.collectionWindow: Interviews, participant observation, and direct observation were reported for 13-17 December 2013. This is a short historical fishery-profile window, not a current fish survey.
reportedScope.respondentsAndMethods: 71 purposively selected artisanal/municipal fisherfolk; semi-structured interviews, observation, and focus-group discussions. The article reports catch composition and gear/boat profile, including hook-and-line and fish-pot/trap use; it is not a standardized station-based ichthyofaunal survey.
reportedScope.richnessCountDiscrepancy: The abstract reports 31 different target-fish species; the Results section says 29 commercially important species including finfish and squid; the Conclusion again says 31 fish and invertebrate species. The paper does not resolve these differing counts in the accessible text.
reportedScope.taxonomyLimit: The abstract and searchable text give common names for the most common catch groups and do not provide binomial identifications for them. Do not translate these names into scientific species without reviewing the complete table and obtaining a defensible local-name crosswalk.
reportedScope.otherReportedMeasures: The paper reports catch per unit effort and fisherfolk/boat profiles for the four barangays. Those figures are historical, gear- and respondent-specific, and are not current catchability guidance.

crossSourceAssessment.habitatScope: Coastal marine fishery profile, not an inland freshwater inventory. Do not merge its reported catches with river or lake records.
crossSourceAssessment.timeAndSamplingLimit: The December 2013 field window and purposive respondent sample cannot establish current occupancy, annual abundance, or present-day catch trends.
crossSourceAssessment.taxonomyReadiness: No scientific-name checklist was normalized. Common names can be broad or locally variable, and the paper's 29/31 count discrepancy remains unresolved.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Useful fisheries-context source only. It does not provide verified catch locations, complete voucher-linked scientific names, current safety/legal rules, or bait/diet recommendations.

rightsReview.status: The official journal record states that the article is licensed Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
rightsReview.handling: Citation and concise factual summary retained with attribution. No full table, article pages, or unverified local-name-to-scientific-name mapping copied into the app data.

disposition.reason: Historical respondent-based coastal fishery data use common names, contain a 29-versus-31 richness discrepancy, and lack a validated scientific-name and location crosswalk.

nextActions: Review the full Table 1 at original resolution and seek the authors' exact scientific names, spelling, per-barangay breakdown, and resolution of the 29/31 count discrepancy; do not send an inquiry without explicit authorization.
Retain this as a coastal fishery-history source separate from present species occurrences, user catchability, and inland-water evidence.
Continue the Eastern Visayas freshwater and marine source sweep, including Biliran and unreviewed Leyte/Samar waters.

sources.supports: Official journal record: authors, citation, abstract, publication date, study summary, and CC BY 4.0 license.

Full 11-page 2014 article text reviewed for the 13-17 December 2013 methodology, four barangays, mixed interview/observation design, 29-versus-31 discrepancy, common-name catch descriptions, and historical limits. This is a mirror of the article, not the primary publisher record.
